question_text: What safety adjustments may be necessary when loading a motorcycle?

options.text: Increase the tyre pressure
Adjust the damping/suspension
Increase the tank volume

correct_answers.text: Increase the tyre pressure
Adjust the damping/suspension

comment: When increasing the load on your motorcycle, make sure to increase the tire pressure and adjust the chassis/suspension

question_text: What should you especially consider when travelling with luggage?

options.text: The recommended top speed given in the vehicle manufacturer's operating manual
The affect of the changed centre of gravity on road handling
The increased susceptibility to side wind

correct_answers.text: The recommended top speed given in the vehicle manufacturer's operating manual
The affect of the changed centre of gravity on road handling
The increased susceptibility to side wind

comment: Adding luggage to your motorcycle will impact its behavior on the road. The additional weight will change the center of gravity of the motorcycle. It will increase the impact of side wind on the motorcycle. Make sure you do not exceed the maximum speed recommended by your manufacturer for driving with luggage.

question_text: Where should you stow heavy luggage?

options.text: In the tank-top bag
Stow equally on the left and right, and as deep as possible in the panniers
In the handlebar bag

correct_answers.text: In the tank-top bag
Stow equally on the left and right, and as deep as possible in the panniers

comment: You should place heavy luggage as close as possible to the center of gravity of your motorcycle to least impact its behavior. Make sure to place it either in the tank-top bag or equally distributed and deep in the panniers.

question_text: How does incorrect loading affect driving stability?

options.text: To heavy tail-loading causes the motorcycle to shimmy and swing
Unequally distributed loading can have a negative effect on driving stability when braking
Has no effect

correct_answers.text: To heavy tail-loading causes the motorcycle to shimmy and swing
Unequally distributed loading can have a negative effect on driving stability when braking

comment: Incorrectly loading your motorcycle will make your motorcycle less stable. It will make it less stable when braking and could make it vibrate or swing

question_text: What must you be aware of when loading a truck with trailer (truck-trailer)?

options.text: The total length of the truck-trailer including load may not exceed 20.75 m
The load must be distributed in such a way so as not to interfere with the operational safety of the truck-trailer
Heavy goods should be positioned as high up as possible

correct_answers.text: The total length of the truck-trailer including load may not exceed 20.75 m
The load must be distributed in such a way so as not to interfere with the operational safety of the truck-trailer

comment: The total length of the train (lorry with trailer) and its load must not 20.75 m passing and the charge is to be distributed so that the operational reliability of the train is not affected and you thus endangering any other participants of road traffic.

question_text: What is the maximum permissible length of a truck with trailer, including load?
comment: The charge of the truck, including trailer must be 20.75 meters long at most.

question_text: You are carrying an additionally attached piece of luggage on your motorbike. What should you take into account?

options.text: Any possible maximum speed recommendations made by the vehicle manufacturer
Any change in the centre of gravity of the motorbike
Any change in the motorbike’s susceptibility to side winds

correct_answers.text: Any possible maximum speed recommendations made by the vehicle manufacturer
Any change in the centre of gravity of the motorbike
Any change in the motorbike’s susceptibility to side winds

comment:
Because of the luggage, your motorbike has a larger surface area to attack, so it is more susceptible to crosswinds. The extra weight also shifts the centre of gravity of your motorbike. You should therefore make sure that the luggage is evenly distributed and adjust your riding behaviour accordingly.
There may be recommendations from the vehicle manufacturer as to how you should adjust your speed to the load. You should follow these. You will find them in the owner's manual.

question_text: How does an improperly stowed load affect the driving stability of a motorbike?

options.text: A heavy load placed on the rear causes the motorbike to wobble and sway at high speeds
A load placed on one side only negatively affects the handling
Light-weight luggage in the tank bag makes skidding more probable

correct_answers.text: A heavy load placed on the rear causes the motorbike to wobble and sway at high speeds
A load placed on one side only negatively affects the handling

comment:
Too heavy a load at the rear of the motorbike puts too little weight on the front tyres and steering. This makes it easier for the bike to wobble and oscillate. Differently loaded sides have a negative effect on stability and handling. The motorbike will lean more towards the heavier side when braking or cornering.
Light luggage in the tank bag does not affect the riding stability of the motorbike.

question_text: What might be needed when a motorcycle is fully loaded?

options.text: An adjustment of the tyre inflation pressure
An adjustment of the chassis
An adjustment of the rear-view mirrors

correct_answers.text: An adjustment of the tyre inflation pressure
An adjustment of the chassis
An adjustment of the rear-view mirrors

comment: If the motorbike is fully loaded, the load exerts more pressure on the tyres. You should therefore check the tyre inflation pressure. The weight of the load could push the chassis down further and must therefore be readjusted. If the load extends beyond the motorbike, you should also readjust the rear view mirrors.

question_text: Carrying a rucksack while cycling can affect the handling of your two-wheeler. What can the consequences be?

options.text: A greater susceptibility to side wind
A displacement of the centre of gravity
An improvement in the manoeuvrability

correct_answers.text: A greater susceptibility to side wind
A displacement of the centre of gravity

comment: By carrying a backpack, you offer a larger surface for crosswinds to attack. Carrying a backpack also shifts your center of gravity upwards. This means you can't steer as quickly.

question_text: What do white plates with a black "A" on a truck mean?

options.text: - is transporting waste materials
- is transporting dangerous goods
- is driven by a beginner

correct_answers.text: - is transporting waste materials

comment: A truck with white plates marked with a black "A" transports litter. The white plates with a black "A" must be clearly visible both at the front and at the back of the truck.

question_text: What must you bear in mind if you want to carry luggage on the roof of your car?

options.text: The roadhandling characteristics are adversely affected
The permissible total mass must not be exceeded
The maximum roof load stipulated by the car manufacturer (owner's manual) must not be exceeded

correct_answers.text: The roadhandling characteristics are adversely affected
The permissible total mass must not be exceeded
The maximum roof load stipulated by the car manufacturer (owner's manual) must not be exceeded

comment: Luggage on the roof changes the center of gravity of your vehicle upwards. This has a significant influence on the driving characteristics of the car. The driving characteristics are worse, especially in curves. The vehicle is wind-prone. It must be ensured that the permissible roof load and total mass are not exceeded.

question_text: What must you reckon with when transporting luggage on the roof of your car?

options.text: The vehicle inclines more on bends
The vehicle's susceptibility to side wind is greater
The vehicle's roadhandling is improved on account of the higher centre of gravity

correct_answers.text: The vehicle inclines more on bends
The vehicle's susceptibility to side wind is greater

comment: The luggage on the roof changes the center of gravity of the vehicle - it is raised. This increases the danger of tipping over and the aerodynamic drag increases. As a result, your vehicle is more sensitive to crosswind and air pressure when a wheel or truck overtakes you. In curves the driving stability also deteriorates due to the higher center of gravity. Your vehicle will tilt more.

question_text: What must you do when transporting bicycles on the roof of your car?

options.text: Safely attach holding device and bicycles
Avoid driving at high speed
Regularly check the fixing devices

correct_answers.text: Safely attach holding device and bicycles
Avoid driving at high speed
Regularly check the fixing devices

comment: Bicycles on the roof require special attention: think of safety regulations and careful attachment. Check the fastenings regularly during driving breaks. Loads on the roof change the center of gravity of the vehicle, they lift it. The driving quality deteriorates especially in curves. Avoid high speeds.

question_text: What must you check when transporting bicycles on a rear-mounted support system?

options.text: Whether, according to the manufacturer's instructions, the system is adequate for the vehicle
Whether system and bicycles are fixed safely
Whether lighting equipment or number plate are covered

correct_answers.text: Whether, according to the manufacturer's instructions, the system is adequate for the vehicle
Whether system and bicycles are fixed safely
Whether lighting equipment or number plate are covered

comment: Check if the rear carry system is securely fastened. Likewise, the attachment of bicycles is to be checked. If illuminating devices or the license plate is obscured, technical equipment must be installed at the end of the vehicle system for adequate lighting and/or to attach the license plate number. Back-heavy loading changes the center of gravity of the vehicle. Check the distribution of the load.

question_text: How must a load be marked in darkness or bad visibility when it extends laterally more than 40 cm beyond the side lights of the vehicle?

options.text: By a white light to the front
By a red light to the back
By switching on the hazard warning lights

correct_answers.text: By a white light to the front
By a red light to the back

comment: In the dark or in poor visibility conditions, a cargo that laterally protrudes more than 40 cm beyond the marker lights of the vehicle must be marked with additional lights. These are to be attached laterally no more than 40 cm from the edge and no more than 1.5 m above the roadway. For the front, a white lamp is required, for the back you need to install a red light. The hazard lights must not be switched on by you as a car driver while driving.

question_text: What is the maximum height allowed above the roadway for a red light marking a load extending to the back?
comment: The maximum height for attaching the lamp is 1.5 meters. This is to ensure that the marking is in the field of vision of other road users. If the red light is higher above the road, it could be overlooked.

question_text: Up to what height is a load not allowed to project over the front of the vehicle?
comment: The red lamp, which marks the rear projecting cargo, may be installed at a maximum height of 2.50 m. If it were higher, other road users might oversee it. To prevent a hazard, a maximum height of 2.50 m is set.

question_text: Under what conditions is a load allowed to project over the front of a vehicle?

options.text: If the load does not project over more than 50 cm and is above a height of 2.50 m
If the load is marked with a red light

correct_answers.text: If the load does not project over more than 50 cm and is above a height of 2.50 m

comment: If the cargo is fastened above a height of 2.50 m, it may protrude up to 50 cm from the front of the vehicle. This regulation is intended to reduce the danger and risk of injury from rear-end collisions with cargo. In general, cargo should always be carefully secured so that it can neither slip nor fall.

question_text: During a break you find out that one of the lashing straps has torn. What do you do?

options.text: Continue your trip after the lashing strap has been replaced
Continue your trip when the load is secured by other sufficient securing means
Continue your trip because a slipping load will be caught by the side panels

correct_answers.text: Continue your trip after the lashing strap has been replaced
Continue your trip when the load is secured by other sufficient securing means

comment: As a car driver, you must ensure that your cargo is properly secured throughout the journey. With a defective strap, you may only continue your journey if proper securing of the cargo is ensured by other securing devices. If this is not the case, you must not continue your journey.

question_text: Do the requirements for properly securing of loads apply to all small transporters?

options.text: They apply to all small transporters
They only apply to small transporters with open loading space
They only apply to small transporters without separation wall to the loading space

correct_answers.text: They apply to all small transporters

comment: Without exception, the requirements for proper securing of the load apply to all vans. Back-heavy loading shifts the center of gravity of the vehicle to the back. As a result, the front wheel is no longer sufficiently burdened and the grip deteriorates. This promotes dangerous pendular movements.

question_text: What can help with friction-locked load securing?

options.text: Lashing straps
Anti-slip mats
Lashing chains

correct_answers.text: Lashing straps
Anti-slip mats
Lashing chains

comment:
In force-locking load securing, the transported goods are pressed onto the loading surface by means of lashing. This type of lashing is also known as tie-down lashing.
The load usually stands freely on the loading surface and is only secured by the increased force applied. In most cases, the frictional force between the loading surface and the load is increased.
The load is secured with the aid of load securing equipment such as lashing straps, lashing chains, anti-slip mats or cover nets and with the aid of attachment points on the loading surface.
This prevents the load from slipping.

question_text: What should be taken into consideration when selecting load-securing lashing equipment?

The available lashing points

Among other things, the face and shape of the load are decisive for the selection of suitable and necessary lashing equipment. 
Equally important are the requirements of the vehicle, such as the permissible payload and the attachment points.

question_text: You want to secure your load by lashing it down. What should you bear in mind?

options.text: - regularly check the tension of the lashing equipment
- only secure dimensionally stable loads by lashing them down
- choose the smallest possible lashing angle

correct_answers.text: - regularly check the tension of the lashing equipment
- only secure dimensionally stable loads by lashing them down

comment: When lashing down, the load is pressed onto the loading area using lashing devices to increase the friction force and prevent slipping. It is important to check the tension of the lashing devices, as the necessary contact force and thus the required friction can only be achieved with sufficient tension. In addition, this method is only suitable for dimensionally stable loads; flexible goods can deform under the tension, which means that the pre-tensioning force is lost and load securing is no longer guaranteed.
